    "id": "dsid_465e8f67162348549c350e62072c564d",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/product/private-deployments/network-evidence-mini-ux-and-rollback-lane-prd.json",

    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/google_drive",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"network-evidence-mini-ux-and-rollback-lane-prd\",\n  \"owner\": \"Priya Desai\",\n  \"drive_area\": \"shared_drives\",\n  \"path\": \"shared_drives/product/private-deployments\",\n  \"doc_type\": \"doc\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-01-12\",\n  \"last_modified\": \"2025-02-03\",\n  \"collaborators\": [\n    \"Marcus Lee\",\n    \"Chen Wu\",\n    \"Ellen Rivera\"\n  ],\n  \"team\": \"product-private-deployments\",\n  \"status\": \"draft\",\n  \"tags\": [\n    \"audit\",\n    \"ux\",\n    \"rollback\",\n    \"telemetry\",\n    \"customer-network\"\n  ],\n  \"linked_artifacts\": [\n    \"CONFLUENCE-PRD-8792\",\n    \"JIRA-PDP-4123\",\n    \"github.com/redwood-inference/ops-playbooks/pull/78\"\n  ],\n  \"body\": \"Purpose and context:\\nThis is an early PRD sketch for a compact network evidence handoff UX and a lightweight rollback lane aimed at customer-managed networking within Private deployments. The goal is to reduce on-call friction during network changes while providing minimal, verifiable audit artifacts that satisfy common SOC/infra audits without forcing full heavy-weight evidence bundles for every small change.\\n\\nWhy this exists (problem statement):\\n- Customers running Redwood Private often push small firewall/peering changes that require operator sign-off and produce large audit payloads (costly to store and slow to review).\\n- On-call and operator teams want a quick way to confirm changes and trigger a safe rollback if telemetry shows regressions.\\n- Security/compliance teams want cryptographic continuity (proof-of-change) and a compact searchable index for postmortems.\\n- Current designs create a binary choice: full attestation (heavy) or no evidence (risky). We need a middle path.\\n\\nPrimary goals (MUST):\\n- Define a compact evidence artifact (mini-evidence) that captures the minimal fields needed for verification and forensic replay.\\n- Provide operator UX flows for \\\"approve-with-quick-evidence\\\" and \\\"approve-with-rollback-lane\\\" integrated into the onboarding console and CLI.\\n- Implement sample-based audit retention that keeps full evidence for a fraction of changes and compact artifacts for all.\\n- Ensure artifacts are signed with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) or with delegated attestation tokens, depending on deployment mode.\\n\\nSecondary goals (SHOULD):\\n- Developer-friendly API to fetch summarized evidence and reconstruct a timeline for a change window.\\n- First-pass analytics on rollback triggers: detect patterns and provide recommended safety thresholds.\\n- Low-bandwidth option for on-prem customers where evidence upload may be deferred but anchored.\\n\\nUser personas:\\n- Customer Network Operator (CNO): makes and reviews changes. Needs fast sign-off and an easy rollback trigger.\\n- Customer Security Auditor (CSA): needs verifiable chain-of-proof, searchable compact index for investigations.\\n- Redwood SRE/Support: occasionally investigates incidents across customers; needs a consistent minimal artifact shape to triage faster.\\n\\nKey user stories:\\n- As a CNO, I can approve a VPC-peering change with a single signed mini-evidence artifact and a checkbox to create a rollback-lane for 30 minutes.\\n- As a CNO, I can trigger an automated rollback from the console within the defined rollback window; the action emits a rollback evidence artifact.\\n- As a CSA, I can query a compact index (time range + change id) and retrieve a signed summary plus pointers to full evidence if retained.\\n- As Redwood SRE, I can optionally request a full evidence pull for a given change id when investigating anomalies; the request is gated and audited.\\n\\nFunctional requirements (high level):\\n1) Mini-evidence artifact schema (compact):\\n   - change_id (uuid), timestamp (ISO8601), actor (email/orig-system), diff_summary (text, <= 512 chars), risk_score (float 0-1), rollback_token (opaque), signature (base64), evidence_retention_level (enum: full|mini|none), verification_anchor (sha256 digest or KMS reference).\\n   - The schema must be serializable as a newline-delimited JSON for easy streaming.\\n\\n2) Rollback lane primitives:\\n   - When a change is approved with rollback enabled, a rollback_token is issued that can be used to invoke an idempotent rollback API endpoint.\\n   - Rollback tokens expire (configurable, default 30m). Triggering rollback generates a rollback-evidence artifact.\\n   - Rollback endpoints are rate-limited and require both token + operator confirmation for high-risk changes.\\n\\n3) Sampling and retention policy:\\n   - By default keep mini artifacts for all changes for 365 days.\\n   - Sample 1 in N (configurable, default N=20) changes for full evidence retention (payloads, snapshots).\\n   - Allow customer to opt into higher sampling or pin specific change_ids for permanent archival.\\n\\n4) Signing and anchoring:\\n   - Support two modes: customer-KMS signing (preferred for Private) and Redwood-signed attestations for hosted-assist operations.\\n   - All signatures must include a key-id and public key reference stored in the tenant metadata.\\n\\n5) UX/Console flows:\\n   - Approve change modal with: \\\"quick-evidence\\\" summary, toggle: enable rollback (30m/1h/4h), optional free-text justification, and checkbox 'anchor now' to request immediate full evidence capture (may cost extra).\\n   - Timeline view for each change showing mini-evidence, sampled full evidence markers, and rollback actions.\\n\\nNon-functional requirements:\\n- Compact artifacts should be <4KB on average.\\n- Verification path (fetch signature, verify with keyref) should complete in <500ms for UI flows.\\n- Storage overhead must be <5% of current logging pipeline costs assuming default sampling.\\n- Backfill/repair: a mechanism to re-anchor evidence after network failures (deferred upload queue).\\n\\nSuccess metrics (proposed):\\n- Mean time to verify a change (CNO) falls below 2 minutes for 90% of approvals.\\n- Fraction of on-call rollbacks successfully executed within window >= 95% for first 30 days.\\n- Customer satisfaction (NPS/CSAT) on onboarding network changes increases by 15 points for pilot customers.\\n- Audit request fulfillment time for compact index < 1 hour for 95% of requests.\\n\\nImplementation sketch (phases):\\nPhase 0 (spike, 2 wks):\\n- Prototype mini-evidence JSON schema and signature flow using local KMS emulator.\\n- Build minimal console modal mock and CLI knob to test operator flows with a subset of customers.\\n\\nPhase 1 (MVP, 6 wks):\\n- Implement artifact generation, signature plumbing for customer-KMS and Redwood-sign mode.\\n- Basic rollback lane: token issuance, rollback endpoint, and evidence emission.\\n- Sampling engine basic config and retention defaults.\\n- Console UX basic modal + timeline placeholder.\\n\\nPhase 2 (hardening, 8 wks):\\n- Integrate deferred upload queue, storage cost telemetry, and compact index for quick queries.\\n- Add HSM/KMS rotation support and key reference UI.\\n- Implement audit request workflow with RBAC and escalation logging.\\n\\nOpen questions and trade-offs (to resolve):\\n- Do we allow rollback tokens to be exported to customer automation (webhooks/terraform)? Risks: token leakage. Possible mitigation: scoped tokens, IP allowlist, short TTL.\\n- Sampling rate economics: how to balance storage cost vs. investigator time? Need pricing/commit model.\\n- For on-prem air-gapped installs, can we allow offline anchoring with later reconciliation? Design needed for proof-of-origin if time-separated.\\n- How much free-text justification do auditors actually need vs structured fields? Extra fields increase artifact size.\\n\\nSafety and compliance notes:\\n- All consented data fields must honor tenant data retention policy.\\n- Signatures and keys are part of customer security review; include KMS attestability documentation in the final PRD.\\n\\nNext steps (immediate):\\n- Schedule 1hr sync with infra and SRE to validate rollback endpoint constraints (Marcus/Chen/Ellen).\\n- Create spike tickets: PDP-4123 (mini-evidence spike), PDP-4124 (rollback token proto).\\n- Identify two pilot customers (one cloud VPC, one on-prem) and prepare test plan.\\n\\nNotes to self / TODOs (rough):\\n- Draft minimal audit index API (search by actor/change_id/range) and include cost model.\\n- Align with legal on signature acceptability for audits in EU/UK jurisdictions.\\n- Add sample mini-evidence payloads to the Confluence prototyping page.\\n\\nRecent references and links:\\n- see linked artifacts above for the working spike threads.\\n- sketch: github.com/redwood-inference/prototypes/mini-evidence\\n\\nEnd of draft.\\n\\n(Free-form roughness intentionally included \\u2014 looking for product + infra feedback on rollback semantics and sampling economics.)\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"body\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_465e8f67162348549c350e62072c564d\"\n}",

{
  "title": "network-evidence-mini-ux-and-rollback-lane-prd",
  "owner": "Priya Desai",
  "drive_area": "shared_drives",
  "path": "shared_drives/product/private-deployments",
  "doc_type": "doc",
  "created_at": "2025-01-12",
  "last_modified": "2025-02-03",
  "collaborators": [
    "Marcus Lee",
    "Chen Wu",
    "Ellen Rivera"
  ],
  "team": "product-private-deployments",
  "status": "draft",
  "tags": [
    "audit",
    "ux",
    "rollback",
    "telemetry",
    "customer-network"
  ],
  "linked_artifacts": [
    "CONFLUENCE-PRD-8792",
    "JIRA-PDP-4123",
    "github.com/redwood-inference/ops-playbooks/pull/78"
  ],
  "body": "Purpose and context:
This is an early PRD sketch for a compact network evidence handoff UX and a lightweight rollback lane aimed at customer-managed networking within Private deployments. The goal is to reduce on-call friction during network changes while providing minimal, verifiable audit artifacts that satisfy common SOC/infra audits without forcing full heavy-weight evidence bundles for every small change.

Why this exists (problem statement):
- Customers running Redwood Private often push small firewall/peering changes that require operator sign-off and produce large audit payloads (costly to store and slow to review).
- On-call and operator teams want a quick way to confirm changes and trigger a safe rollback if telemetry shows regressions.
- Security/compliance teams want cryptographic continuity (proof-of-change) and a compact searchable index for postmortems.
- Current designs create a binary choice: full attestation (heavy) or no evidence (risky). We need a middle path.

Primary goals (MUST):
- Define a compact evidence artifact (mini-evidence) that captures the minimal fields needed for verification and forensic replay.
- Provide operator UX flows for "approve-with-quick-evidence" and "approve-with-rollback-lane" integrated into the onboarding console and CLI.
- Implement sample-based audit retention that keeps full evidence for a fraction of changes and compact artifacts for all.
- Ensure artifacts are signed with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) or with delegated attestation tokens, depending on deployment mode.

Secondary goals (SHOULD):
- Developer-friendly API to fetch summarized evidence and reconstruct a timeline for a change window.
- First-pass analytics on rollback triggers: detect patterns and provide recommended safety thresholds.
- Low-bandwidth option for on-prem customers where evidence upload may be deferred but anchored.

User personas:
- Customer Network Operator (CNO): makes and reviews changes. Needs fast sign-off and an easy rollback trigger.
- Customer Security Auditor (CSA): needs verifiable chain-of-proof, searchable compact index for investigations.
- Redwood SRE/Support: occasionally investigates incidents across customers; needs a consistent minimal artifact shape to triage faster.

Key user stories:
- As a CNO, I can approve a VPC-peering change with a single signed mini-evidence artifact and a checkbox to create a rollback-lane for 30 minutes.
- As a CNO, I can trigger an automated rollback from the console within the defined rollback window; the action emits a rollback evidence artifact.
- As a CSA, I can query a compact index (time range + change id) and retrieve a signed summary plus pointers to full evidence if retained.
- As Redwood SRE, I can optionally request a full evidence pull for a given change id when investigating anomalies; the request is gated and audited.

Functional requirements (high level):
1) Mini-evidence artifact schema (compact):
   - change_id (uuid), timestamp (ISO8601), actor (email/orig-system), diff_summary (text, <= 512 chars), risk_score (float 0-1), rollback_token (opaque), signature (base64), evidence_retention_level (enum: full|mini|none), verification_anchor (sha256 digest or KMS reference).
   - The schema must be serializable as a newline-delimited JSON for easy streaming.

2) Rollback lane primitives:
   - When a change is approved with rollback enabled, a rollback_token is issued that can be used to invoke an idempotent rollback API endpoint.
   - Rollback tokens expire (configurable, default 30m). Triggering rollback generates a rollback-evidence artifact.
   - Rollback endpoints are rate-limited and require both token + operator confirmation for high-risk changes.

3) Sampling and retention policy:
   - By default keep mini artifacts for all changes for 365 days.
   - Sample 1 in N (configurable, default N=20) changes for full evidence retention (payloads, snapshots).
   - Allow customer to opt into higher sampling or pin specific change_ids for permanent archival.

4) Signing and anchoring:
   - Support two modes: customer-KMS signing (preferred for Private) and Redwood-signed attestations for hosted-assist operations.
   - All signatures must include a key-id and public key reference stored in the tenant metadata.

5) UX/Console flows:
   - Approve change modal with: "quick-evidence" summary, toggle: enable rollback (30m/1h/4h), optional free-text justification, and checkbox 'anchor now' to request immediate full evidence capture (may cost extra).
   - Timeline view for each change showing mini-evidence, sampled full evidence markers, and rollback actions.

Non-functional requirements:
- Compact artifacts should be <4KB on average.
- Verification path (fetch signature, verify with keyref) should complete in <500ms for UI flows.
- Storage overhead must be <5% of current logging pipeline costs assuming default sampling.
- Backfill/repair: a mechanism to re-anchor evidence after network failures (deferred upload queue).

Success metrics (proposed):
- Mean time to verify a change (CNO) falls below 2 minutes for 90% of approvals.
- Fraction of on-call rollbacks successfully executed within window >= 95% for first 30 days.
- Customer satisfaction (NPS/CSAT) on onboarding network changes increases by 15 points for pilot customers.
- Audit request fulfillment time for compact index < 1 hour for 95% of requests.

Implementation sketch (phases):
Phase 0 (spike, 2 wks):
- Prototype mini-evidence JSON schema and signature flow using local KMS emulator.
- Build minimal console modal mock and CLI knob to test operator flows with a subset of customers.

Phase 1 (MVP, 6 wks):
- Implement artifact generation, signature plumbing for customer-KMS and Redwood-sign mode.
- Basic rollback lane: token issuance, rollback endpoint, and evidence emission.
- Sampling engine basic config and retention defaults.
- Console UX basic modal + timeline placeholder.

Phase 2 (hardening, 8 wks):
- Integrate deferred upload queue, storage cost telemetry, and compact index for quick queries.
- Add HSM/KMS rotation support and key reference UI.
- Implement audit request workflow with RBAC and escalation logging.

Open questions and trade-offs (to resolve):
- Do we allow rollback tokens to be exported to customer automation (webhooks/terraform)? Risks: token leakage. Possible mitigation: scoped tokens, IP allowlist, short TTL.
- Sampling rate economics: how to balance storage cost vs. investigator time? Need pricing/commit model.
- For on-prem air-gapped installs, can we allow offline anchoring with later reconciliation? Design needed for proof-of-origin if time-separated.
- How much free-text justification do auditors actually need vs structured fields? Extra fields increase artifact size.

Safety and compliance notes:
- All consented data fields must honor tenant data retention policy.
- Signatures and keys are part of customer security review; include KMS attestability documentation in the final PRD.

Next steps (immediate):
- Schedule 1hr sync with infra and SRE to validate rollback endpoint constraints (Marcus/Chen/Ellen).
- Create spike tickets: PDP-4123 (mini-evidence spike), PDP-4124 (rollback token proto).
- Identify two pilot customers (one cloud VPC, one on-prem) and prepare test plan.

Notes to self / TODOs (rough):
- Draft minimal audit index API (search by actor/change_id/range) and include cost model.
- Align with legal on signature acceptability for audits in EU/UK jurisdictions.
- Add sample mini-evidence payloads to the Confluence prototyping page.

Recent references and links:
- see linked artifacts above for the working spike threads.
- sketch: github.com/redwood-inference/prototypes/mini-evidence

End of draft.

(Free-form roughness intentionally included — looking for product + infra feedback on rollback semantics and sampling economics.)",
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "body"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_465e8f67162348549c350e62072c564d"
}

    "title": "Interleaved KV-cache staleness detection and tenant-protect remediation for canary regressions",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/linear",
    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"ENG-764214\",\n  \"team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"title\": \"Interleaved KV-cache staleness detection and tenant-protect remediation for canary regressions\",\n  \"status\": \"In Progress\",\n  \"priority\": \"P0\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-03-10\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-03-12\",\n  \"creator\": \"Maya Chen\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Luca Martinez\",\n  \"project\": \"Runtime Reliability\",\n  \"cycle\": \"2026-W10\",\n  \"estimate\": \"8\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2026-03-20\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"canary\",\n    \"kv-cache\",\n    \"rollback\",\n    \"customer-impact\",\n    \"hotfix\"\n  ],\n  \"dependencies\": [\n    \"ENG-657123\"\n  ],\n  \"customer_impact\": \"high\",\n  \"release\": \"runtime-1.24\",\n  \"security_review_required\": \"false\",\n  \"description\": \"Objective: Detect and recover from a class of canary regressions caused by interleaved/heterogeneous KV-cache states between model variants and runtime kernel selections. These regressions surface as silent quality drops for a subset of tenants after a canary rollout (often in mixed-hosted/dedicated deployments) where cached KV state is incompatible with the newly served model variant. The goal of this ticket is to add deterministic detection signals, an automated tenant-protect remediation path, and an operator runbook that minimizes blast radius and customer impact across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.\",\n  \"acceptance_criteria\": [\n    \"A1: Alerting rule that detects per-tenant drop in similarity/quality metric (delta > 10% over 15m) correlated with increased token rejection or malformed logits must fire within 5 minutes\",\n    \"A2: Automated remediation that quarantines the affected tenant slice (redirects to last-known-good variant) within 2 minutes of confirmed detection for Hosted and Dedicated environments\",\n    \"A3: Playbook for Private deployments that provides operator CLI steps and idempotent cache-resync script with clear rollback commands\",\n    \"A4: End-to-end QA scenario that reproduces KV-cache mismatch on staging, validates detection, and confirms rollback path restores baseline metrics to within 2% of pre-rollout quality\",\n    \"A5: Post-deployment telemetry dashboard and incident timeline generator linked from Console runtime page\"\n  ],\n  \"runbook_steps\": [\n    \"1) Triage: Use console alert to identify tenant slices with quality delta > threshold. Confirm regression by running a deterministic prompt set for the tenant and comparing normalized similarity scores to baseline.\",\n    \"2) Fast mitigation (Hosted/Dedicated): Toggle routing policy for affected tenant to 'pin:previous-variant' via routing API (route-change-idempotent). Immediately trigger targeted KV-cache invalidation for the tenant slice (invalidate-prefix: tenant_id:kvcache:*)\",\n    \"3) If quality does not recover within 3 minutes: perform directional rollback of canary slice (reduce canary weight to 0%) and activate fallback model variant cluster. Notify customers in affected slice with templated comms.\",\n    \"4) Private deployments: Notify on-call infra lead, provide operator script (resync_kv.sh) to flush and resync caches from persist layer. If operator cannot run within SLA window, instruct customer to switch traffic to previous image via their orchestrator template (docs included).\",\n    \"5) Post-mitigation: capture full diff of outputs for sample corpus, store the corrupted KV entries for root cause analysis, and escalate to model-onboarding if pattern suggests model-layer incompatibility.\",\n    \"6) Permanent fix: decide between deterministic cache versioning (bump KV namespace on model minor/compat changes) or compatibility shim in runtime. Implement feature flag guarded change and schedule gradual rollout with heavier telemetry.\",\n    \"7) Communication and closure: send internal incident summary to SRE/PM/Support and external brief to impacted customers within 24 hours. Attach reproducible test case and remediation timeline.\"\n  ],\n  \"rollback_plan\": [\n    \"Hosted: automated rollback - pin traffic to stable model variant and invalidate affected KV prefixes; provide temporary traffic-shaping to limit new writes to KV cache during recovery.\",\n    \"Dedicated: orchestration service will stop canary instances and reassign capacity to stable pool; perform cache reconciliation using reconcile-worker job. If reconciliation fails, rollback host image and clear per-tenant caches.\",\n    \"Private: provide operator-run rollback artifact with exact image tag and docker-compose/k8s manifest; include ordered steps to restore DB-backed KV snapshot and restart runtime with 'cache-safe' flag.\",\n    \"Fallback: if rollback not possible immediately, automatically reduce batch size and enable strict deterministic decoding to reduce variance and surface regression symptoms less frequently while remediation proceeds.\"\n  ],\n  \"telemetry_signals\": [\n    \"Per-tenant quality delta (similarity/regression_score) over 1m/5m/15m windows\",\n    \"Token acceptance/rejection rate changes by tenant and route\",\n    \"KV-cache hit/miss ratio and per-prefix error rates\",\n    \"Model variant assignment shifts (routing changes) and steady-state serving kernel selection histogram\",\n    \"Request latency P50/P95/P99 changes for affected tenants\"\n  ],\n  \"comms_template\": \"We detected an anomaly impacting a subset of requests tied to the recent model rollout. We've redirected your traffic to the previous stable variant and are performing a cache resync. Expected service restoration: within 30 minutes. If you continue to see degraded outputs after that time, please reply with example prompts and request IDs. We apologize for the disruption and will follow up with a post-incident summary.\",\n  \"links\": [\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4872 - kv-cache-detection-agent\",\n    \"https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RUNTIME/KV+Cache+Compatibility+Design\",\n    \"https://console.redwood.com/dashboards/runtime/kv-cache-regressions\",\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-scripts/blob/main/resync_kv.sh\"\n  ],\n  \"comments\": [\n    \"2026-03-10 Maya Chen: Initial triage complete \\u2014 reproducer identified in staging. Suspect mismatch between kernel-optimizations and cache serialization format introduced in runtime-1.24.\",\n    \"2026-03-11 Luca Martinez: Instrumented additional telemetry (per-tenant hit/miss and serialization errors). Patch merged to staging (PR #4872). Running canary to verify detection firing thresholds.\",\n    \"2026-03-12 Support (Alina Gupta): Drafted customer notification template and queued for review by PM. Identified two enterprise tenants in dedicated clusters that will be notified first.\",\n    \"2026-03-12 QA (Diego Alvarez): Reproducer run shows detection alert fires at 6m; need to tighten threshold to 4m to meet acceptance criteria A1. Updating alert rule and rerunning tests.\"\n  ],\n  \"decision_log\": [\n    \"2026-03-10: Decided to prioritize detection + automated tenant pin over broad immediate rollback to reduce blast radius.\",\n    \"2026-03-11: Rejected short-term solution of blanket cache flush because it risks invalidating warm caches for high-throughput tenants and may increase latency; moved to targeted prefix invalidation.\",\n    \"2026-03-12: Agreed to add cache-namespace bumping to model-onboarding checklist as medium-term compatibility guarantee.\"\n  ],\n  \"follow_up_tasks\": [\n    \"Add cache-namespace version into model manifest and enforce bump on incompatible changes (owner: Model-Onboarding)\",\n    \"Build dashboard tile that surfaces affected tenant count and time-to-recover for KV-cache regressions (owner: Observability)\",\n    \"Draft runbook tabletop exercise for canary-cached-state regressions and include SRE/Support/PM participants (owner: Reliability)\",\n    \"Post-incident writeup and RCA to be published within 72 hours of incident closure (owner: Incident Lead)\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"acceptance_criteria\",\n    \"runbook_steps\",\n    \"rollback_plan\",\n    \"telemetry_signals\",\n    \"comms_template\",\n    \"comments\",\n    \"decision_log\",\n    \"follow_up_tasks\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_c15505d76b084fbb9704ba282a1f5196\"\n}",

document.title: Interleaved KV-cache staleness detection and tenant-protect remediation for canary regressions
document.content:
{
  "key": "ENG-764214",
  "team": "engineering",
  "title": "Interleaved KV-cache staleness detection and tenant-protect remediation for canary regressions",
  "status": "In Progress",
  "priority": "P0",
  "created_at": "2026-03-10",
  "updated_at": "2026-03-12",
  "creator": "Maya Chen",
  "assignee": "Luca Martinez",
  "project": "Runtime Reliability",
  "cycle": "2026-W10",
  "estimate": "8",
  "due_date": "2026-03-20",
  "labels": [
    "canary",
    "kv-cache",
    "rollback",
    "customer-impact",
    "hotfix"
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    "ENG-657123"
  ],
  "customer_impact": "high",
  "release": "runtime-1.24",
  "security_review_required": "false",
  "description": "Objective: Detect and recover from a class of canary regressions caused by interleaved/heterogeneous KV-cache states between model variants and runtime kernel selections. These regressions surface as silent quality drops for a subset of tenants after a canary rollout (often in mixed-hosted/dedicated deployments) where cached KV state is incompatible with the newly served model variant. The goal of this ticket is to add deterministic detection signals, an automated tenant-protect remediation path, and an operator runbook that minimizes blast radius and customer impact across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.",
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    "A1: Alerting rule that detects per-tenant drop in similarity/quality metric (delta > 10% over 15m) correlated with increased token rejection or malformed logits must fire within 5 minutes",
    "A2: Automated remediation that quarantines the affected tenant slice (redirects to last-known-good variant) within 2 minutes of confirmed detection for Hosted and Dedicated environments",
    "A3: Playbook for Private deployments that provides operator CLI steps and idempotent cache-resync script with clear rollback commands",
    "A4: End-to-end QA scenario that reproduces KV-cache mismatch on staging, validates detection, and confirms rollback path restores baseline metrics to within 2% of pre-rollout quality",
    "A5: Post-deployment telemetry dashboard and incident timeline generator linked from Console runtime page"
  ],
  "runbook_steps": [
    "1) Triage: Use console alert to identify tenant slices with quality delta > threshold. Confirm regression by running a deterministic prompt set for the tenant and comparing normalized similarity scores to baseline.",
    "2) Fast mitigation (Hosted/Dedicated): Toggle routing policy for affected tenant to 'pin:previous-variant' via routing API (route-change-idempotent). Immediately trigger targeted KV-cache invalidation for the tenant slice (invalidate-prefix: tenant_id:kvcache:*)",
    "3) If quality does not recover within 3 minutes: perform directional rollback of canary slice (reduce canary weight to 0%) and activate fallback model variant cluster. Notify customers in affected slice with templated comms.",
    "4) Private deployments: Notify on-call infra lead, provide operator script (resync_kv.sh) to flush and resync caches from persist layer. If operator cannot run within SLA window, instruct customer to switch traffic to previous image via their orchestrator template (docs included).",
    "5) Post-mitigation: capture full diff of outputs for sample corpus, store the corrupted KV entries for root cause analysis, and escalate to model-onboarding if pattern suggests model-layer incompatibility.",
    "6) Permanent fix: decide between deterministic cache versioning (bump KV namespace on model minor/compat changes) or compatibility shim in runtime. Implement feature flag guarded change and schedule gradual rollout with heavier telemetry.",
    "7) Communication and closure: send internal incident summary to SRE/PM/Support and external brief to impacted customers within 24 hours. Attach reproducible test case and remediation timeline."
  ],
  "rollback_plan": [
    "Hosted: automated rollback - pin traffic to stable model variant and invalidate affected KV prefixes; provide temporary traffic-shaping to limit new writes to KV cache during recovery.",
    "Dedicated: orchestration service will stop canary instances and reassign capacity to stable pool; perform cache reconciliation using reconcile-worker job. If reconciliation fails, rollback host image and clear per-tenant caches.",
    "Private: provide operator-run rollback artifact with exact image tag and docker-compose/k8s manifest; include ordered steps to restore DB-backed KV snapshot and restart runtime with 'cache-safe' flag.",
    "Fallback: if rollback not possible immediately, automatically reduce batch size and enable strict deterministic decoding to reduce variance and surface regression symptoms less frequently while remediation proceeds."
  ],
  "telemetry_signals": [
    "Per-tenant quality delta (similarity/regression_score) over 1m/5m/15m windows",
    "Token acceptance/rejection rate changes by tenant and route",
    "KV-cache hit/miss ratio and per-prefix error rates",
    "Model variant assignment shifts (routing changes) and steady-state serving kernel selection histogram",
    "Request latency P50/P95/P99 changes for affected tenants"
  ],
  "comms_template": "We detected an anomaly impacting a subset of requests tied to the recent model rollout. We've redirected your traffic to the previous stable variant and are performing a cache resync. Expected service restoration: within 30 minutes. If you continue to see degraded outputs after that time, please reply with example prompts and request IDs. We apologize for the disruption and will follow up with a post-incident summary.",
  "links": [
    "https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4872 - kv-cache-detection-agent",
    "https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RUNTIME/KV+Cache+Compatibility+Design",
    "https://console.redwood.com/dashboards/runtime/kv-cache-regressions",
    "https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-scripts/blob/main/resync_kv.sh"
  ],
  "comments": [
    "2026-03-10 Maya Chen: Initial triage complete \u2014 reproducer identified in staging. Suspect mismatch between kernel-optimizations and cache serialization format introduced in runtime-1.24.",
    "2026-03-11 Luca Martinez: Instrumented additional telemetry (per-tenant hit/miss and serialization errors). Patch merged to staging (PR #4872). Running canary to verify detection firing thresholds.",
    "2026-03-12 Support (Alina Gupta): Drafted customer notification template and queued for review by PM. Identified two enterprise tenants in dedicated clusters that will be notified first.",
    "2026-03-12 QA (Diego Alvarez): Reproducer run shows detection alert fires at 6m; need to tighten threshold to 4m to meet acceptance criteria A1. Updating alert rule and rerunning tests."
  ],
  "decision_log": [
    "2026-03-10: Decided to prioritize detection + automated tenant pin over broad immediate rollback to reduce blast radius.",
    "2026-03-11: Rejected short-term solution of blanket cache flush because it risks invalidating warm caches for high-throughput tenants and may increase latency; moved to targeted prefix invalidation.",
    "2026-03-12: Agreed to add cache-namespace bumping to model-onboarding checklist as medium-term compatibility guarantee."
  ],
  "follow_up_tasks": [
    "Add cache-namespace version into model manifest and enforce bump on incompatible changes (owner: Model-Onboarding)",
    "Build dashboard tile that surfaces affected tenant count and time-to-recover for KV-cache regressions (owner: Observability)",
    "Draft runbook tabletop exercise for canary-cached-state regressions and include SRE/Support/PM participants (owner: Reliability)",
    "Post-incident writeup and RCA to be published within 72 hours of incident closure (owner: Incident Lead)"
  ],
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "description",
    "acceptance_criteria",
    "runbook_steps",
    "rollback_plan",
    "telemetry_signals",
    "comms_template",
    "comments",
    "decision_log",
    "follow_up_tasks"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_c15505d76b084fbb9704ba282a1f5196"
}

document.title: 3891234567 paging rollout streaming client compat incident
document.content:
{
  "channel": "incidents",
  "thread_ts": "3891234567",
  "first_message_ts": "3891234567",
  "last_message_ts": "3891234867",
  "participants": [
    "incident-bot",
    "maya (oncall)",
    "sam (eng)",
    "jonah (sre)",
    "eva (prodops)",
    "leigh (release)",
    "akash (cs)",
    "deploy-bot"
  ],
  "thread": "incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: paging-service errors spike (502 / stream failures) after deploy 2026-03-15T02:10Z. Estimated error rate 9% across streaming endpoints. Auto-escalation to #incidents.

maya (oncall): seeing it too — most failures are streaming clients hitting paging endpoints during long-poll. Quick check: canary group shows 15% errors, stable group ~0.5%.

sam (eng): rolling deploy 2026-03-15 02:04Z included SDK header change: `X-Stream-Proto: v2` and paging server now rejects legacy `v1` frames with 400 -> becomes 502 on our proxy path.

jonah (sre): confirmed in logs:
```
proxy[proxy-4] 2026-03-15T02:12:31Z ERROR downstream 502 "upstream response error" path=/v1/stream/paging request_id=abcd-1234
server[paging-1] 2026-03-15T02:12:30Z WARN unexpected-frame-version: received v1 header, expected v2
```

maya (oncall): customers reporting: BetaCorp webhooks failing, EchoNotify message fanout delayed. Akash can you surface which accounts?

akash (cs): pulling list now. Early look: BetaCorp (high volume), EchoNotify (medium), ~7 smaller integrations. I'll assemble a short customer-facing note if we have mitigation plan.

eva (prodops): mitigation options: 1) kill flag for new header acceptance so service accepts both v1 and v2; 2) rollback the SDK deploy to canary; 3) apply header rewrite at proxy to translate v1->v2 for affected clients. Fastest is kill-flag or proxy rewrite. Rollback is slower.

leigh (release): we can flip the feature flag `ff:accept_v1_stream_header=false` -> default was set true in canary. I'll prepare the FF kill switch; need oncall approval to flip.

maya (oncall): do it. Flip flag now and watch.

deploy-bot: Feature flag update requested by leigh (release) at 2026-03-15T02:18Z: `accept_v1_stream_header = false` -> changed to `true` (previously true in canary, setting to false will re-enable legacy acceptance). Change-id: ff-20260315-7

leigh (release): url: https://flags.redwood/ff-20260315-7 — flip executed.

jonah (sre): watching metrics — error rate on canary dropped from 15% -> 1.2% within 45s. Proxy 502s trending down.

sam (eng): adding a temporary proxy rewrite in envoy for older clients to ensure no more choked frames. Quick config snippet we pushed to the canary proxy tier: 
```
- match: { header: ":path", prefix: "/v1/stream/paging" }
  request_headers_to_add:
    - header: "X-Stream-Proto"
      value: "v2"
      append_action: OVERWRITE_IF_EXISTS_OR_ADD
```
Deployed to proxy-canary pool.

maya (oncall): looks stable on canary and rolling to remainder of fleet. Thanks.

akash (cs): drafting customer message: 
"We detected a regression impacting streaming paging for some SDK versions after a deploy. We have applied a mitigation (feature flag and proxy rewrite) and services are recovering. No data loss; retries recommended. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline."

leigh (release): marking rollout paused and starting rollback plan for SDK release 4.6.0 -> 4.5.x for non-critical customers. Canary is paused.

sam (eng): root cause summary so far: server-side strictness was increased to reject `X-Stream-Proto: v1` frames during validation; the rollout included a change in SDK that started sending `v2` semantics from clients compiled with new headers, but proxy path for mixed-traffic caused legacy clients to be interpreted incorrectly. We need a compatibility shim and expanded integration tests.

jonah (sre): oncall handoff to sam in 30m. Action items for next shift:
- monitor 1m, 5m error rates for /v1/stream/paging
- validate proxy rewrite across all regions: eu-west-1, us-east-1, ap-southeast-1
- coordinate with release to push a compatibility patch to paging service (accept both frames cleanly)

maya (oncall): handing off. Full notes: incident start 2026-03-15T02:10Z, mitigation (flag + proxy rewrite) applied 02:18-02:20Z, error rate returned to baseline by 02:23Z for canary and 02:31Z for global.

sam (eng): taking over. I'll keep this thread updated.

akash (cs): customers notified via status page and targeted email to affected accounts at 02:40Z. Internal CS playbook: offer immediate retry guidance and temporary bump in rate limits for BetaCorp if needed.

leigh (release): postmortem owners: sam (eng), jonah (sre), leigh (release). Timeline and communications draft due by EOD.

maya (oncall): quick retrospective notes in thread: 
- missing compatibility tests for mixed v1/v2 streaming frames in canary gating.
- feature flag default flipped too early in rollout path.
- our rollout checklist should include a proxy compatibility smoke test.

sam (eng): immediate follow-ups assigned:
1) patch paging service to accept old frames without rejecting (PR queued: https://git.redwood/paging/merge/4821) — target hotfix in next 2 hours.
2) add end-to-end smoke tests for SDK<->proxy<->paging for header permutations.
3) coordinate a minor SDK re-release with clear semver and client opt-in.

jonah (sre): ops follow-ups:
- confirm proxy rewrite is present in all regions (in progress)
- run synthetic traffic for top 10 customers to verify recovery (in progress)

akash (cs): compiling customer impact summary: ~2.3% of total streaming requests affected during the window, top affected: BetaCorp (~38% of impacted), EchoNotify (~12%). No data loss reports.

deploy-bot: deploy rollouts paused for sdk-client-4.6.0 by leigh at 2026-03-15T02:25Z.

sam (eng): updating PR with test vectors. I'll follow up with a release plan for a compatibility patch and a staged re-rollout with stronger canary checks.

maya (oncall): thanks team. handing final notes to sam. If things degrade again, page me.

sam (eng): acknowledged. Leaving monitoring dashboards: https://dash.redwood/incidents/3891234567

jonah (sre): Handoff complete at 2026-03-15T02:48Z.

-- end of thread --",
  "title_field_name": "channel",
  "content_field_names": [
    "thread"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_3860a24fd9f5408ea9d1cb678d366033"
}

    "title": "PrimeBank EAP: model-freeze & export window prioritization request",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/gmail",
    "content": "{\n  \"thread_id\": \"thread-20260912-00072\",\n  \"mailbox_owner\": \"laura_bennett\",\n  \"subject\": \"PrimeBank EAP: model-freeze & export window prioritization request\",\n  \"participants_internal\": [\n    \"laura_bennett\",\n    \"rishi_malhotra\",\n    \"jasmine_liu\",\n    \"ben_carter\"\n  ],\n  \"participants_external\": [\n    \"Asha Menon <primebank-ops@primebank.com>\",\n    \"Liam O'Connor <pmc-contracts@primebank.com>\"\n  ],\n  \"message_count\": \"4\",\n  \"first_email_at\": \"2026-09-12T09:18:00-07:00\",\n  \"last_email_at\": \"2026-09-15T14:02:00-07:00\",\n  \"thread_type\": \"sales\",\n  \"related_account\": \"PrimeBank\",\n  \"deal_id\": \"PB-2026-0473\",\n  \"region\": \"us\",\n  \"has_attachments\": \"true\",\n  \"attachments\": [\n    \"primebank_eap_spec_v1.pdf\",\n    \"redwood_impact_estimate.xlsx\"\n  ],\n  \"related_links\": [\n    \"https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567\",\n    \"https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/ENG-9125\"\n  ],\n  \"messages\": [\n    \"From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>\\\\nTo: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>\\\\nCc: Asha Menon <primebank-ops@primebank.com>\\\\nDate: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700\\\\nSubject: PrimeBank EAP: model-freeze & export window prioritization request\\\\n\\\\nTeam \\u2014 quick ask on a high-impact EAP for PrimeBank (Enterprise, strategic). They have a binding go-live condition in their procurement that requires us to provide deterministic model snapshots and an export window for their auditors plus a one-time export of inference logs for the onboarding audit. Without this, legal will withhold final signature (deal PB-2026-0473).\\\\n\\\\nI attached the spec they supplied (primebank_eap_spec_v1.pdf) and a rough cost/effort estimate (redwood_impact_estimate.xlsx). Key asks from the customer thread are:\\\\n- Deterministic model freeze (ability to pin exact model weights/quantization and ensure identical outputs for a given prompt set)\\\\n- Secure export window for one-time logs + periodic snapshot exports (S3-compatible encrypted bundle)\\\\n- Audit-friendly retention + checksum verification\\\\n\\\\nBusiness ask: can Product/Eng triage and let us know by EOD Tue (2026-09-14) whether this is possible in the next two sprints or if we need to offer the dedicated-instance workaround (routing PrimeBank to a dedicated residency with export support) as the only go-live path?\\\\n\\\\nTradeoffs are understood \\u2014 performance/latency, storage, and long-term maintenance. If we can scope an MVP (minimal deterministic freeze + one export) that can land in ~4 weeks, sales can commit to a partial contract signature and push for an accelerated take in Q4.\\\\n\\\\nProposed next steps:\\\\n1) Product to confirm scope and gating criteria (what 'deterministic' means operationally).\\\\n2) Eng to provide a high-level effort estimate and blockers.\\\\n3) If no faster path, confirm whether we can allocate a dedicated instance as stopgap and what the net cost is.\\\\n\\\\nThanks \\u2014 attaching spec & estimate. This is a time-sensitive procurement condition.\\\\n\\\\n\\u2014 Laura Bennett\\\\nSr. Account Lead, Strategic Accounts\\\\nRedwood Inference\\\\n\",\n    \"From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>\\\\nTo: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>\\\\nCc: Asha Menon <primebank-ops@primebank.com>\\\\nDate: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 08:43:00 -0700\\\\nSubject: Re: PrimeBank EAP: model-freeze & export window prioritization request\\\\n\\\\nThanks Laura \\u2014 important ask. A few clarifying questions before Eng sizes:\\\\n- Does PrimeBank require cryptographic hash verification of the model weights (to prove immutability), or is an API-level pinned-version enough?\\\\n- For the export window: are they asking for a one-off export for onboarding plus scheduled exports, or a single one-time export only?\\\\n\\\\nFrom a product perspective, the \\\\\\\"deterministic freeze\\\\\\\" needs a clear acceptance test: a prompt set + seed + KV cache state that we can replay and get identical token streams. That implies capturing tokenizer/version, quantization parameters, and exact kernel selection. If they want a cryptographic artifact bundle, that raises compliance + storage questions.\\\\n\\\\nJasmine \\u2014 can you list the primary engineering dependencies (KV cache snapshot, model artifact immutability, export pipeline encryption) and a ballpark effort? If we can decompose into an MVP that only supports: (A) pin model build+quantization for inference, (B) one-time export of last-30-days logs with encryption, that might be doable faster.\\\\n\\\\nIf Engineering needs >2 sprints, we should prepare the dedicated-instance fallback and price it into commercial terms.\\\\n\\\\nRishi\\\\nDirector, Product Management\\\\n\",\n    \"From: jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>\\\\nTo: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>\\\\nCc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Asha Menon <primebank-ops@primebank.com>\\\\nDate: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700\\\\nSubject: Re: PrimeBank EAP: model-freeze & export window prioritization request\\\\n\\\\nOn Mon, Sep 14, 2026 at 08:43 AM Rishi M wrote:\\\\n> From a product perspective, the \\\\\\\"deterministic freeze\\\\\\\" needs a clear acceptance test...\\\\n\\\\nQuick technical readout \\u2014 keeping it high level:\\\\nPrimary engineering pieces and rough complexity:\\\\n- Model artifact immutability: medium. We already have build provenance; adding an exportable signed bundle (weights + quant params + tokenizer hash) is ~2 dev-weeks + 1 security review.\\\\n- Deterministic replay acceptance test: medium-high. We need a small harness to capture RNG seeds, KV cache snapshot, and a deterministic inference runner for replay across releases \\u2014 ~3-4 dev-weeks.\\\\n- Export pipeline for logs/snapshots (encrypted S3 bundle with checksums): low-medium if leveraging existing export infra \\u2014 ~2 dev-weeks plus infra tasks for encrypted transient storage.\\\\n- Operational gating: canaries, can rollbacks, and retention policies \\u2014 ~1 dev-week for policies + config UI work if Product needs an admin knob.\\\\n\\\\nSo conservative timeline for an MVP (pin build + one-time export + replay harness) is ~6 weeks of focused work (approx 3 sprints) given current capacity. If we prioritize it into the next sprint (force-off other items) we might compress to ~4 weeks but that needs exec sign-off.\\\\n\\\\nWorkarounds:\\\\n- Dedicated instance path: stand up a pinned model on a dedicated pool for PrimeBank and expose an export API. Pros: fastest (2 weeks) and operationally simple; cons: higher recurring cost and more manual work for us.\\\\n- Hybrid: deliver the signed artifact export first (2-3 weeks) while we build the replay harness in parallel. That could satisfy procurement if they accept artifact + planned replay timeline.\\\\n\\\\nI've attached a preliminary effort breakdown (redwood_impact_estimate.xlsx) referenced by Laura. If Product can confirm acceptance criteria (exact hashes vs pinned-version), we'll finalize a Jira ticket and scope the sprints.\\\\n\\\\nJasmine Liu\\\\nStaff Engineer, Serving Runtime\\\\nRedwood Inference\\\\n\",\n    \"From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>\\\\nTo: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>\\\\nCc: Asha Menon <primebank-ops@primebank.com>, Liam O'Connor <pmc-contracts@primebank.com>\\\\nDate: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 14:02:00 -0700\\\\nSubject: Re: PrimeBank EAP: model-freeze & export window prioritization request\\\\n\\\\nLooping to push for prioritization \\u2014 this is a near-term revenue milestone (PB-2026-0473). Commercial notes: PrimeBank has signaled they will split signature (60% now) if we can commit to the artifact export + a defined delivery plan for the replay harness. They've asked for a decision by COB Thu (2026-09-16).\\\\n\\\\nOptions for Product/Eng decision:\\\\n1) Commit to MVP roadmap (artifact export + one-time logs export) in 4 weeks, with replay harness in subsequent sprint. We market this as a two-phase delivery.\\\\n2) Approve dedicated-instance fallback (2 weeks) and price it into the deal \\u2014 gets them live quickly but increases TCO and complicates scale precedent.\\\\n3) Decline and ask Sales to renegotiate procurement terms (risk: deal stalls).\\\\n\\\\nIf Product/Eng can sign option (1) or (2) by Thu COB, I'll update PrimeBank legal and push the partial signature through. I'm prepared to shift two sprint slots (swap with a lower-priority internal item) to accelerate.\\\\n\\\\nRequested ask: Product (Rishi) please confirm acceptance criteria (hash vs pinned artifact) and Jasmine please confirm if you can target the compressed path (4 weeks) if we reallocate sprint capacity.\\\\n\\\\nThanks \\u2014 Ben\\\\nBen Carter\\\\nHead of Enterprise Sales\\\\nRedwood Inference\\\\n\\\\nAttachments: redwood_impact_estimate.xlsx\\\\nRelated links: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567 | Jira ENG-9125\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"subject\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"messages\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_741491ba728d4fc683ce530bd3627c19\"\n}",

# Private Deployment Rollback — Fast Lane

Owner: SRE / release on-call  
Scope: Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem)  
Goal: restore the last known-good revision quickly through a minimal, reversible path.

## Preconditions

Before every rollout, record the change ID, operator, stable image or bundle digest, manifest/config digest, database and KV snapshot IDs, and the tested route or feature-flag reversal. Pre-stage the prior signed bundle and retain the previous control plane read-only. Do not begin if the previous artifact or snapshot cannot be resolved.

## Trigger

Rollback immediately when any one of these occurs during the change window:

- an error-rate or latency SLO breach persists for two consecutive observation intervals;
- a functional smoke test fails;
- data or KV-cache integrity is uncertain;
- streaming/client compatibility regresses;
- the operator cannot explain a partial apply.

Pause the rollout first. Avoid oscillation: after rollback begins, do not re-advance without a new change review.

## Fast rollback path

1. Declare the incident/change ID and name one rollback operator and one on-call approver.
2. Freeze further rollout and writes that could make the old revision incompatible.
3. Capture one compact, signed pre-action record: timestamp, actor, change ID, current and target digests, snapshot IDs, trigger metric/smoke failure, rollback method, and approval.
4. Use the least invasive tested reversal:
   - flip the kill flag or gateway route to the stable pool;
   - for a private runtime regression, apply the exact prior signed image/manifest and start with the cache-safe flag;
   - for an infrastructure partial apply, re-apply the archived prior Terraform plan; never reconstruct it from memory.
5. Restore the DB/KV snapshot only when integrity or schema compatibility requires it. Otherwise preserve state and reconcile after traffic is safe.
6. Run the fixed smoke set and verify error rate, p95/p99 latency, saturation, routing, and representative deterministic prompts for two consecutive intervals.
7. Emit a signed rollback evidence record and keep the incident open for reconciliation.

## Stop conditions and escalation

Stop automation and require incident commander plus customer operator approval if the stable digest is unavailable, signature verification fails, the snapshot is missing, rollback would cross a schema boundary, or the first reversal worsens health. Preserve customer control of keys and do not export payloads from the private environment.

## Reconciliation and close

Compare desired stable state with every node, route, config, model/tokenizer/quantization digest, DB schema, and KV snapshot. Quarantine mismatches. Close only after the fleet converges, the compact records verify, deferred evidence is anchored, and the incident timeline links the trigger, approval, actions, and outcome.

## Required evidence sources

This contract is grounded in:

- Google Drive: `/knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/product/private-deployments/network-evidence-mini-ux-and-rollback-lane-prd.json` (`dsid_465e8f67162348549c350e62072c564d`)

3. Capture one compact, signed pre-action record: timestamp, actor, change ID, current and target digests, snapshot IDs, trigger metric/smoke failure, rollback method, and approval.
4. Use the least invasive tested reversal:
   - flip the kill flag or gateway route to the stable pool;
   - for a private runtime regression, apply the exact prior signed image/manifest and start with the cache-safe flag;
   - for an infrastructure partial apply, re-apply the archived prior Terraform plan; never reconstruct it from memory.
5. Restore the DB/KV snapshot only when integrity or schema compatibility requires it. Otherwise preserve state and reconcile after traffic is safe.
6. Run the fixed smoke set and verify error rate, p95/p99 latency, saturation, routing, and representative deterministic prompts for two consecutive intervals.
7. Emit a signed rollback evidence record and keep the incident open for reconciliation.

## Stop conditions and escalation

Stop automation and require incident commander plus customer operator approval if the stable digest is unavailable, signature verification fails, the snapshot is missing, rollback would cross a schema boundary, or the first reversal worsens health. Preserve customer control of keys and do not export payloads from the private environment.

## Reconciliation and close

Compare desired stable state with every node, route, config, model/tokenizer/quantization digest, DB schema, and KV snapshot. Quarantine mismatches. Close only after the fleet converges, the compact records verify, deferred evidence is anchored, and the incident timeline links the trigger, approval, actions, and outcome.

# Private Deployment Rollback — Evidence-Gated Contract

Owner: SRE incident commander  
Scope: Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem)  
Contract: a rollback is a staged, approved state transition to a cryptographically identified stable revision, followed by deterministic validation and reconciliation.

## 1. Prepare and admit the change

No rollout starts until the release owner and customer operator record:

- change ID, maintenance window, deployment and tenant IDs;
- exact signed image/bundle, model weights, tokenizer, quantization, config and manifest digests;
- immutable desired-state snapshot ID plus DB and KV snapshot IDs;
- archived prior Terraform plan or tested route/flag reversal;
- staged traffic plan, smoke/eval set, SLO trigger thresholds, hysteresis window, rollback lane expiry and approvers.

Verify signatures with the customer KMS/HSM or delegated attestation key. Failure of provenance, snapshot resolution, backup validation, or approval is a hard stop.

## 2. Stage the rollout

Advance through internal/private staging, then a bounded canary, then successive cohorts. At every stage compare error rate, p95/p99 latency, saturation, client/streaming compatibility, data integrity and deterministic prompt results with the stable baseline. Require the release owner and customer operator to approve each advance; add security approval when keys, IAM, network policy or audit logging change. Keep the previous control plane read-only and its artifacts pre-staged.

## 3. Trigger and contain

Pause immediately on any functional failure, integrity uncertainty, unexplained partial apply, signature/evidence failure, or sustained SLO breach across the configured hysteresis window. A hard integrity or compatibility failure needs no waiting window. Freeze incompatible writes, retain customer data in the private boundary, declare the incident/change ID, and capture the pre-rollback snapshot.

## 4. Evidence gate

Before mutation, create a signed compact evidence record (target average below 4 KB) containing timestamp, actor, change/deployment IDs, source and target digests, diff summary, risk/trigger, metric and smoke references, snapshot IDs, rollback method, approval identities, retention level and verification anchor. Customer-KMS signing is preferred. If an air-gapped site cannot upload, anchor locally and queue reconciliation; absence of a verifiable local record blocks rollback except for an immediate life-safety/security containment directed by the incident commander, which must be documented locally.

## 5. Approval gate

Normal rollback requires incident commander/release owner and customer operator approval. Security also approves key, IAM, network-policy and audit-log changes. An emergency kill-flag or route reversal may proceed with on-call plus customer operator approval when delay increases customer harm; it cannot waive provenance or the post-action record.

## 6. Execute staged rollback

1. Prefer the smallest tested reversal: kill flag or route to the stable pool.
2. Validate a bounded cohort. If healthy for two consecutive intervals, drain remaining traffic to stable.
3. For runtime faults, apply the exact prior signed image/manifest with cache-safe mode.
4. For infrastructure partial apply, re-apply the archived prior Terraform plan; do not reverse-engineer state.
5. Restore DB/KV snapshots only when integrity or compatibility requires it.
6. If any step worsens health, stop automation, quarantine affected nodes and escalate to the incident commander and customer operator.

Every command is idempotent or carries a unique operation ID.

## 7. Validation gate

Do not declare recovery until two consecutive intervals pass the fixed smoke/eval set and error, latency, saturation, routing, compatibility and integrity checks. Verify deterministic replay against the pinned weights, quantization, tokenizer, RNG inputs and relevant KV snapshot. Record exceptions rather than silently changing the test set.

## 8. Reconciliation gate

Compare stored desired state with every reported node, route, config, model digest, DB schema and KV state. Quarantine mismatches, dry-apply repairs against the stable snapshot, then re-apply with backoff only after validation. Re-anchor deferred evidence and issue a signed rollback artifact linking pre/post snapshots, approvals, actions, checks and outcome. Keep the incident open until convergence and evidence verification complete.

## 9. Re-advance

A rollback ends the release attempt. Re-advance requires a new change ID, corrected artifact, full admission checks and approvals; never bounce automatically across a threshold.

              "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Private Deployment Rollback\nSource: Aisha Bello reviewed candidate\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/private-deployment-rollback.md\nWorkspace: task/aisha-bello/rollback-evidence-gate-v3\n\n# Private Deployment Rollback — Evidence-Gated Contract\n\nOwner: SRE incident commander  \nScope: Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem)  \nContract: a rollback is a staged, approved state transition to a cryptographically identified stable revision, followed by deterministic validation and reconciliation.\n\n## 1. Prepare and admit the change\n\nNo rollout starts until the release owner and customer operator record:\n\n- change ID, maintenance window, deployment and tenant IDs;\n- exact signed image/bundle, model weights, tokenizer, quantization, config and manifest digests;\n- immutable desired-state snapshot ID plus DB and KV snapshot IDs;\n- archived prior Terraform plan or tested route/flag reversal;\n- staged traffic plan, smoke/eval set, SLO trigger thresholds, hysteresis window, rollback lane expiry and approvers.\n\nVerify signatures with the customer KMS/HSM or delegated attestation key. Failure of provenance, snapshot resolution, backup validation, or approval is a hard stop.\n\n## 2. Stage the rollout\n\nAdvance through internal/private staging, then a bounded canary, then successive cohorts. At every stage compare error rate, p95/p99 latency, saturation, client/streaming compatibility, data integrity and deterministic prompt results with the stable baseline. Require the release owner and customer operator to approve each advance; add security approval when keys, IAM, network policy or audit logging change. Keep the previous control plane read-only and its artifacts pre-staged.\n\n## 3. Trigger and contain\n\nPause immediately on any functional failure, integrity uncertainty, unexplained partial apply, signature/evidence failure, or sustained SLO breach across the configured hysteresis window. A hard integrity or compatibility failure needs no waiting window. Freeze incompatible writes, retain customer data in the private boundary, declare the incident/change ID, and capture the pre-rollback snapshot.\n\n## 4. Evidence gate",

              "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Private Deployment Rollback\nSource: Aisha Bello reviewed candidate\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/private-deployment-rollback.md\nWorkspace: task/aisha-bello/rollback-evidence-gate-v3\n\n, signature/evidence failure, or sustained SLO breach across the configured hysteresis window. A hard integrity or compatibility failure needs no waiting window. Freeze incompatible writes, retain customer data in the private boundary, declare the incident/change ID, and capture the pre-rollback snapshot.\n\n## 4. Evidence gate\n\nBefore mutation, create a signed compact evidence record (target average below 4 KB) containing timestamp, actor, change/deployment IDs, source and target digests, diff summary, risk/trigger, metric and smoke references, snapshot IDs, rollback method, approval identities, retention level and verification anchor. Customer-KMS signing is preferred. If an air-gapped site cannot upload, anchor locally and queue reconciliation; absence of a verifiable local record blocks rollback except for an immediate life-safety/security containment directed by the incident commander, which must be documented locally.\n\n## 5. Approval gate\n\nNormal rollback requires incident commander/release owner and customer operator approval. Security also approves key, IAM, network-policy and audit-log changes. An emergency kill-flag or route reversal may proceed with on-call plus customer operator approval when delay increases customer harm; it cannot waive provenance or the post-action record.\n\n## 6. Execute staged rollback\n\n1. Prefer the smallest tested reversal: kill flag or route to the stable pool.\n2. Validate a bounded cohort. If healthy for two consecutive intervals, drain remaining traffic to stable.\n3. For runtime faults, apply the exact prior signed image/manifest with cache-safe mode.\n4. For infrastructure partial apply, re-apply the archived prior Terraform plan; do not reverse-engineer state.\n5. Restore DB/KV snapshots only when integrity or compatibility requires it.\n6. If any step worsens health, stop automation, quarantine affected nodes and escalate to the incident commander and customer operator.\n\nEvery command is idempotent or carries a unique operation ID.\n\n## 7. Validation gate\n\nDo not declare recovery until two consecutive intervals pass the fixed smoke/eval set and error, latency, saturation, routing, compatibility and integrity checks. Verify deterministic replay against the pinned weights, quantization, tokenizer, RNG inputs and relevant KV snapshot. Record exceptions rather than silently changing the test set.\n\n## 8.             "content": "# Private Deployment Rollback — Evidence-Gated Contract\n\nOwner: SRE incident commander  \nScope: Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem)  \nContract: a rollback is a staged, approved state transition to a cryptographically identified stable revision, followed by deterministic validation and reconciliation.\n\n## 1. Prepare and admit the change\n\nNo rollout starts until the release owner and customer operator record:\n\n- change ID, maintenance window, deployment and tenant IDs;\n- exact signed image/bundle, model weights, tokenizer, quantization, config and manifest digests;\n- immutable desired-state snapshot ID plus DB and KV snapshot IDs;\n- archived prior Terraform plan or tested route/flag reversal;\n- staged traffic plan, smoke/eval set, SLO trigger thresholds, hysteresis window, rollback lane expiry and approvers.\n\nVerify signatures with the customer KMS/HSM or delegated attestation key. Failure of provenance, snapshot resolution, backup validation, or approval is a hard stop.\n\n## 2. Stage the rollout\n\nAdvance through internal/private staging, then a bounded canary, then successive cohorts. At every stage compare error rate, p95/p99 latency, saturation, client/streaming compatibility, data integrity and deterministic prompt results with the stable baseline. Require the release owner and customer operator to approve each advance; add security approval when keys, IAM, network policy or audit logging change. Keep the previous control plane read-only and its artifacts pre-staged.\n\n## 3. Trigger and contain\n\nPause immediately on any functional failure, integrity uncertainty, unexplained partial apply, signature/evidence failure, or sustained SLO breach across the configured hysteresis window. A hard integrity or compatibility failure needs no waiting window. Freeze incompatible writes, retain customer data in the private boundary, declare the incident/change ID, and capture the pre-rollback snapshot.\n\n## 4. Evidence gate\n\nBefore mutation, create a signed compact evidence record (target average below 4 KB) containing timestamp, actor, change/deployment IDs, source and target digests, diff summary, risk/trigger, metric and smoke references, snapshot IDs, rollback method, approval identities, retention level and verification anchor. Customer-KMS signing is preferred. If an air-gapped site cannot upload, anchor locally and queue reconciliation; absence of a verifiable local record blocks rollback except for an immediate life-safety/security containment directed by the incident commander, which must be documented locally.\n\n## 5. Approval gate\n\nNormal rollback requires incident commander/release owner and customer operator approval. Security also approves key, IAM, network-policy and audit-log changes. An emergency kill-flag or route reversal may proceed with on-call plus customer operator approval when delay increases customer harm; it cannot waive provenance or the post-action record.\n\n## 6. Execute staged rollback\n\n1. Prefer the smallest tested reversal: kill flag or route to the stable pool.\n2. Validate a bounded cohort. If healthy for two consecutive intervals, drain remaining traffic to stable.\n3. For runtime faults, apply the exact prior signed image/manifest with cache-safe mode.\n4. For infrastructure partial apply, re-apply the archived prior Terraform plan; do not reverse-engineer state.\n5. Restore DB/KV snapshots only when integrity or compatibility requires it.\n6. If any step worsens health, stop automation, quarantine affected nodes and escalate to the incident commander and customer operator.\n\nEvery command is idempotent or carries a unique operation ID.\n\n## 7. Validation gate\n\nDo not declare recovery until two consecutive intervals pass the fixed smoke/eval set and error, latency, saturation, routing, compatibility and integrity checks. Verify deterministic replay against the pinned weights, quantization, tokenizer, RNG inputs and relevant KV snapshot. Record exceptions rather than silently changing the test set.\n\n## 8. # Private Deployment Rollback — Evidence-Gated Contract

Owner: SRE incident commander  
Scope: Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem)  
Contract: a rollback is a staged, approved state transition to a cryptographically identified stable revision, followed by deterministic validation and reconciliation.

## 1. Prepare and admit the change

No rollout starts until the release owner and customer operator record:

- change ID, maintenance window, deployment and tenant IDs;
- exact signed image/bundle, model weights, tokenizer, quantization, config and manifest digests;
- immutable desired-state snapshot ID plus DB and KV snapshot IDs;
- archived prior Terraform plan or tested route/flag reversal;
- staged traffic plan, smoke/eval set, SLO trigger thresholds, hysteresis window, rollback lane expiry and approvers.

Verify signatures with the customer KMS/HSM or delegated attestation key. Failure of provenance, snapshot resolution, backup validation, or approval is a hard stop.

## 2. Stage the rollout

Advance through internal/private staging, then a bounded canary, then successive cohorts. At every stage compare error rate, p95/p99 latency, saturation, client/streaming compatibility, data integrity and deterministic prompt results with the stable baseline. Require the release owner and customer operator to approve each advance; add security approval when keys, IAM, network policy or audit logging change. Keep the previous control plane read-only and its artifacts pre-staged.

## 3. Trigger and contain

Pause immediately on any functional failure, integrity uncertainty, unexplained partial apply, signature/evidence failure, or sustained SLO breach across the configured hysteresis window. A hard integrity or compatibility failure needs no waiting window. Freeze incompatible writes, retain customer data in the private boundary, declare the incident/change ID, and capture the pre-rollback snapshot.

## 4. Evidence gate

Freeze incompatible writes, retain customer data in the private boundary, declare the incident/change ID, and capture the pre-rollback snapshot.

## 4. Evidence gate

Before mutation, create a signed compact evidence record (target average below 4 KB) containing timestamp, actor, change/deployment IDs, source and target digests, diff summary, risk/trigger, metric and smoke references, snapshot IDs, rollback method, approval identities, retention level and verification anchor. Customer-KMS signing is preferred. If an air-gapped site cannot upload, anchor locally and queue reconciliation; absence of a verifiable local record blocks rollback except for an immediate life-safety/security containment directed by the incident commander, which must be documented locally.

## 5. Approval gate

Normal rollback requires incident commander/release owner and customer operator approval. Security also approves key, IAM, network-policy and audit-log changes. An emergency kill-flag or route reversal may proceed with on-call plus customer operator approval when delay increases customer harm; it cannot waive provenance or the post-action record.

## 6. Execute staged rollback

1. Prefer the smallest tested reversal: kill flag or route to the stable pool.
2. Validate a bounded cohort. If healthy for two consecutive intervals, drain remaining traffic to stable.
3. For runtime faults, apply the exact prior signed image/manifest with cache-safe mode.
4. For infrastructure partial apply, re-apply the archived prior Terraform plan; do not reverse-engineer state.
5. Restore DB/KV snapshots only when integrity or compatibility requires it.
6. If any step worsens health, stop automation, quarantine affected nodes and escalate to the incident commander and customer operator.

Every command is idempotent or carries a unique operation ID.

## 7. Validation gate

Do not declare recovery until two consecutive intervals pass the fixed smoke/eval set and error, latency, saturation, routing, compatibility and integrity checks. Verify deterministic replay against the pinned weights, quantization, tokenizer, RNG inputs and relevant KV snapshot. Record exceptions rather than silently changing the test set.

## 8. Reconciliation gate

Compare stored desired state with every reported node, route, config, model digest, DB schema and KV state. Quarantine mismatches, dry-apply repairs against the stable snapshot, then re-apply with backoff only after validation. A hard integrity or compatibility failure needs no waiting window. Freeze incompatible writes, retain customer data in the private boundary, declare the incident/change ID, and capture the pre-rollback snapshot.\n\n## 4. Evidence gate\n\nBefore mutation, create a signed compact evidence record (target average below 4 KB) containing timestamp, actor, change/deployment IDs, source and target digests, diff summary, risk/trigger, metric and smoke references, snapshot IDs, rollback method, approval identities, retention level and verification anchor. Customer-KMS signing is preferred. If an air-gapped site cannot upload, anchor locally and queue reconciliation; absence of a verifiable local record blocks rollback except for an immediate life-safety/security containment directed by the incident commander, which must be documented locally.\n\n## 5. Approval gate\n\nNormal rollback requires incident commander/release owner and customer operator approval. Security also approves key, IAM, network-policy and audit-log changes. An emergency kill-flag or route reversal may proceed with on-call plus customer operator approval when delay increases customer harm; it cannot waive provenance or the post-action record.\n\n## 6. Execute staged rollback\n\n1. Prefer the smallest tested reversal: kill flag or route to the stable pool.\n2. Validate a bounded cohort. If healthy for two consecutive intervals, drain remaining traffic to stable.\n3. For runtime faults, apply the exact prior signed image/manifest with cache-safe mode.\n4. For infrastructure partial apply, re-apply the archived prior Terraform plan; do not reverse-engineer state.\n5. Restore DB/KV snapshots only when integrity or compatibility requires it.\n6. If any step worsens health, stop automation, quarantine affected nodes and escalate to the incident commander and customer operator.\n\nEvery command is idempotent or carries a unique operation ID.\n\n## 7. Validation gate\n\nDo not declare recovery until two consecutive intervals pass the fixed smoke/eval set and error, latency, saturation, routing, compatibility and integrity checks. Verify deterministic replay against the pinned weights, quantization, tokenizer, RNG inputs and relevant KV snapshot. Record exceptions rather than silently changing the test set.\n\n## 8.
