document.content:
# Private Deployment Rollback — Evidence-Gated Contract

Owner: SRE incident commander  
Scope: Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem)  
Contract: a rollback is a staged, approved state transition to a cryptographically identified stable revision, followed by deterministic validation and reconciliation.

## 1. Prepare and admit the change

No rollout starts until the release owner and customer operator record:

- change ID, maintenance window, deployment and tenant IDs;
- exact signed image/bundle, model weights, tokenizer, quantization, config and manifest digests;
- immutable desired-state snapshot ID plus DB and KV snapshot IDs;
- archived prior Terraform plan or tested route/flag reversal;
- staged traffic plan, smoke/eval set, SLO trigger thresholds, hysteresis window, rollback lane expiry and approvers.

Verify signatures with the customer KMS/HSM or delegated attestation key. Failure of provenance, snapshot resolution, backup validation, or approval is a hard stop.

## 2. Stage the rollout

Advance through internal/private staging, then a bounded canary, then successive cohorts. At every stage compare error rate, p95/p99 latency, saturation, client/streaming compatibility, data integrity and deterministic prompt results with the stable baseline. Require the release owner and customer operator to approve each advance; add security approval when keys, IAM, network policy or audit logging change. Keep the previous control plane read-only and its artifacts pre-staged.

## 3. Trigger and contain

Pause immediately on any functional failure, integrity uncertainty, unexplained partial apply, signature/evidence failure, or sustained SLO breach across the configured hysteresis window. A hard integrity or compatibility failure needs no waiting window. Freeze incompatible writes, retain customer data in the private boundary, declare the incident/change ID, and capture the pre-rollback snapshot.

## 4. Evidence gate

Before mutation, create a signed compact evidence record (target average below 4 KB) containing timestamp, actor, change/deployment IDs, source and target digests, diff summary, risk/trigger, metric and smoke references, snapshot IDs, rollback method, approval identities, retention level and verification anchor. Customer-KMS signing is preferred. If an air-gapped site cannot upload, anchor locally and queue reconciliation; absence of a verifiable local record blocks rollback except for an immediate life-safety/security containment directed by the incident commander, which must be documented locally.

## 5. Approval gate

Normal rollback requires incident commander/release owner and customer operator approval. Security also approves key, IAM, network-policy and audit-log changes. An emergency kill-flag or route reversal may proceed with on-call plus customer operator approval when delay increases customer harm; it cannot waive provenance or the post-action record.

## 6. Execute staged rollback

1. Prefer the smallest tested reversal: kill flag or route to the stable pool.
2. Validate a bounded cohort. If healthy for two consecutive intervals, drain remaining traffic to stable.
3. For runtime faults, apply the exact prior signed image/manifest with cache-safe mode.
4. For infrastructure partial apply, re-apply the archived prior Terraform plan; do not reverse-engineer state.
5. Restore DB/KV snapshots only when integrity or compatibility requires it.
6. If any step worsens health, stop automation, quarantine affected nodes and escalate to the incident commander and customer operator.

Every command is idempotent or carries a unique operation ID.

## 7. Validation gate

Do not declare recovery until two consecutive intervals pass the fixed smoke/eval set and error, latency, saturation, routing, compatibility and integrity checks. Verify deterministic replay against the pinned weights, quantization, tokenizer, RNG inputs and relevant KV snapshot. Record exceptions rather than silently changing the test set.

## 8. Reconciliation gate

Compare stored desired state with every reported node, route, config, model digest, DB schema and KV state. Quarantine mismatches, dry-apply repairs against the stable snapshot, then re-apply with backoff only after validation. Re-anchor deferred evidence and issue a signed rollback artifact linking pre/post snapshots, approvals, actions, checks and outcome. Keep the incident open until convergence and evidence verification complete.

## 9. Re-advance

A rollback ends the release attempt. Re-advance requires a new change ID, corrected artifact, full admission checks and approvals; never bounce automatically across a threshold.

## Authoritative evidence

- Google Drive: `/knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/product/private-deployments/network-evidence-mini-ux-and-rollback-lane-prd.json` (`dsid_465e8f67162348549c350e62072c564d`) — signed compact evidence, rollback lanes, deferred anchoring.
- Linear: `/knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-764214-interleaved-kvcache-staleness-detection-tenant-protect.json` (`dsid_c15505d76b084fbb9704ba282a1f5196`) — exact private rollback artifact, DB/KV restore, cache-safe restart and reconciliation.
- Slack incidents: `/knowledge/company/sources/slack/incidents/3891234567-paging-rollout-streaming-client-compat-incident.json` (`dsid_3860a24fd9f5408ea9d1cb678d366033`) — pause, kill switch, on-call approval, canary validation.
- Gmail: `/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/laura_bennett/20260912-primebank-eap-freeze-export-window-request.json` (`dsid_741491ba728d4fc683ce530bd3627c19`) — immutable signed model bundle and deterministic replay inputs.

# Private Deployment Rollback — Evidence-Gated Contract

Owner: SRE incident commander  
Scope: Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem)  
Contract: a rollback is a staged, approved state transition to a cryptographically identified stable revision, followed by deterministic validation and reconciliation.

## 1. Prepare and admit the change

No rollout starts until the release owner and customer operator record:

- change ID, maintenance window, deployment and tenant IDs;
- exact signed image/bundle, model weights, tokenizer, quantization, config and manifest digests;
- immutable desired-state snapshot ID plus DB and KV snapshot IDs;
- archived prior Terraform plan or tested route/flag reversal;
- staged traffic plan, smoke/eval set, SLO trigger thresholds, hysteresis window, rollback lane expiry and approvers.

Verify signatures with the customer KMS/HSM or delegated attestation key. Failure of provenance, snapshot resolution, backup validation, or approval is a hard stop.

## 2. Stage the rollout

Advance through internal/private staging, then a bounded canary, then successive cohorts. At every stage compare error rate, p95/p99 latency, saturation, client/streaming compatibility, data integrity and deterministic prompt results with the stable baseline. Require the release owner and customer operator to approve each advance; add security approval when keys, IAM, network policy or audit logging change. Keep the previous control plane read-only and its artifacts pre-staged.

## 3. Trigger and contain

Pause immediately on any functional failure, integrity uncertainty, unexplained partial apply, signature/evidence failure, or sustained SLO breach across the configured hysteresis window. A hard integrity or compatibility failure needs no waiting window. Freeze incompatible writes, retain customer data in the private boundary, declare the incident/change ID, and capture the pre-rollback snapshot.

## 4. Evidence gate",

## 1. Prepare and admit the change

## 3. Trigger and contain

Pause immediately on any functional failure, integrity uncertainty, unexplained partial apply, signature/evidence failure, or sustained SLO breach across the configured hysteresis window.               "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Private Deployment Rollback\nSource: Aisha Bello reviewed candidate\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/private-deployment-rollback.md\nWorkspace: task/aisha-bello/rollback-evidence-gate-v3\n\n# Private Deployment Rollback — Evidence-Gated Contract\n\nOwner: SRE incident commander  \nScope: Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem)  \nContract: a rollback is a staged, approved state transition to a cryptographically identified stable revision, followed by deterministic validation and reconciliation.\n\n## 1. Prepare and admit the change\n\nNo rollout starts until the release owner and customer operator record:\n\n- change ID, maintenance window, deployment and tenant IDs;\n- exact signed image/bundle, model weights, tokenizer, quantization, config and manifest digests;\n- immutable desired-state snapshot ID plus DB and KV snapshot IDs;\n- archived prior Terraform plan or tested route/flag reversal;\n- staged traffic plan, smoke/eval set, SLO trigger thresholds, hysteresis window, rollback lane expiry and approvers.\n\nVerify signatures with the customer KMS/HSM or delegated attestation key. Failure of provenance, snapshot resolution, backup validation, or approval is a hard stop.\n\n## 2. Stage the rollout\n\nAdvance through internal/private staging, then a bounded canary, then successive cohorts. At every stage compare error rate, p95/p99 latency, saturation, client/streaming compatibility, data integrity and deterministic prompt results with the stable baseline. Require the release owner and customer operator to approve each advance; add security approval when keys, IAM, network policy or audit logging change. Keep the previous control plane read-only and its artifacts pre-staged.\n\n## 3. Trigger and contain\n\nPause immediately on any functional failure, integrity uncertainty, unexplained partial apply, signature/evidence failure, or sustained SLO breach across the configured hysteresis window. A hard integrity or compatibility failure needs no waiting window. Freeze incompatible writes, retain customer data in the private boundary, declare the incident/change ID, and capture the pre-rollback snapshot.\n\n## 4. Evidence gate",

              "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Private Deployment Rollback\nSource: Aisha Bello reviewed candidate\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/private-deployment-rollback.md\nWorkspace: task/aisha-bello/rollback-evidence-gate-v3\n\n# Private Deployment Rollback — Evidence-Gated Contract\n\nOwner: SRE incident commander  \nScope: Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem)  \nContract: a rollback is a staged, approved state transition to a cryptographically identified stable revision, followed by deterministic validation and reconciliation.\n\n## 1. Prepare and admit the change\n\nNo rollout starts until the release owner and customer operator record:\n\n- change ID, maintenance window, deployment and tenant IDs;\n- exact signed image/bundle, model weights, tokenizer, quantization, config and manifest digests;\n- immutable desired-state snapshot ID plus DB and KV snapshot IDs;\n- archived prior Terraform plan or tested route/flag reversal;\n- staged traffic plan, smoke/eval set, SLO trigger thresholds, hysteresis window, rollback lane expiry and approvers.\n\nVerify signatures with the customer KMS/HSM or delegated attestation key. Failure of provenance, snapshot resolution, backup validation, or approval is a hard stop.\n\n## 2. Stage the rollout\n\nAdvance through internal/private staging, then a bounded canary, then successive cohorts. At every stage compare error rate, p95/p99 latency, saturation, client/streaming compatibility, data integrity and deterministic prompt results with the stable baseline. Require the release owner and customer operator to approve each advance; add security approval when keys, IAM, network policy or audit logging change. Keep the previous control plane read-only and its artifacts pre-staged.\n\n## 3. Trigger and contain\n\nPause immediately on any functional failure, integrity uncertainty, unexplained partial apply, signature/evidence failure, or sustained SLO breach across the configured hysteresis window. A hard integrity or compatibility failure needs no waiting window. Freeze incompatible writes, retain customer data in the private boundary, declare the incident/change ID, and capture the pre-rollback snapshot.\n\n## 4. Evidence gate",

If healthy for two consecutive intervals, drain remaining traffic to stable.\n3. For runtime faults, apply the exact prior signed image/manifest with cache-safe mode.\n4. For infrastructure partial apply, re-apply the archived prior Terraform plan; do not reverse-engineer state.\n5. Restore DB/KV snapshots only when integrity or compatibility requires it.\n6. Validation gate\n\nDo not declare recovery until two consecutive intervals pass the fixed smoke/eval set and error, latency, saturation, routing, compatibility and integrity checks.               "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Private Deployment Rollback\nSource: Aisha Bello reviewed candidate\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/private-deployment-rollback.md\nWorkspace: task/aisha-bello/rollback-evidence-gate-v3\n\n, signature/evidence failure, or sustained SLO breach across the configured hysteresis window. A hard integrity or compatibility failure needs no waiting window. Freeze incompatible writes, retain customer data in the private boundary, declare the incident/change ID, and capture the pre-rollback snapshot.\n\n## 4. Evidence gate\n\nBefore mutation, create a signed compact evidence record (target average below 4 KB) containing timestamp, actor, change/deployment IDs, source and target digests, diff summary, risk/trigger, metric and smoke references, snapshot IDs, rollback method, approval identities, retention level and verification anchor. Customer-KMS signing is preferred. If an air-gapped site cannot upload, anchor locally and queue reconciliation; absence of a verifiable local record blocks rollback except for an immediate life-safety/security containment directed by the incident commander, which must be documented locally.\n\n## 5. Approval gate\n\nNormal rollback requires incident commander/release owner and customer operator approval. Security also approves key, IAM, network-policy and audit-log changes. An emergency kill-flag or route reversal may proceed with on-call plus customer operator approval when delay increases customer harm; it cannot waive provenance or the post-action record.\n\n## 6. Execute staged rollback\n\n1. Prefer the smallest tested reversal: kill flag or route to the stable pool.\n2. Validate a bounded cohort. If healthy for two consecutive intervals, drain remaining traffic to stable.\n3. For runtime faults, apply the exact prior signed image/manifest with cache-safe mode.\n4. For infrastructure partial apply, re-apply the archived prior Terraform plan; do not reverse-engineer state.\n5. Restore DB/KV snapshots only when integrity or compatibility requires it.\n6. If any step worsens health, stop automation, quarantine affected nodes and escalate to the incident commander and customer operator.\n\nEvery command is idempotent or carries a unique operation ID.\n\n## 7. Validation gate\n\nDo not declare recovery until two consecutive intervals pass the fixed smoke/eval set and error, latency, saturation, routing, compatibility and integrity checks. Verify deterministic replay against the pinned weights, quantization, tokenizer, RNG inputs and relevant KV snapshot. Record exceptions rather than silently changing the test set.\n\n## 8. # Evidence-gate candidate review notes (unindexed)

## Gate-cost model

Assumption-only estimate: admission 10–20 min; compact record and signatures 2–5 min; staged reversal 10–30 min; bundle restart 20–60 min if needed; validation and reconciliation 15–30 min. Expected route/flag recovery is roughly 27–65 min; full bundle recovery roughly 47–95 min.

## Unresolved assumptions

- Customer-specific approver matrices and emergency delegations are not centrally enumerated.
- Exact SLO values, interval length and cohort sizes must be supplied by deployment policy.
- Deterministic replay across heterogeneous accelerators may require tolerances rather than byte-identical output.
- Deferred local anchoring format for every air-gapped version needs compatibility confirmation.
- The mini-evidence PRD is draft, so numeric artifact/retention targets remain reviewable constraints.
